title: AI Conferences in San Francisco 2026
seoTitle: AI conferences in San Francisco 2026 | GlobalTechEvents
description: If a friend asked which San Francisco AI conference is still worth booking in 2026, I would not send them to Moscone. As of 2026-10-16 the only one still ahead inside the city is Reverie, one day on November 5 at the Contemporary Jewish Museum, and I would book it only if the work is training data or multimodal models. The multi-day builder weeks I would still book are outside the city: PyTorch Conference and AGNTCon in San Jose, then ODSC in Burlingame.
metaDescription: As of 16 October 2026, Reverie on 5 November is the only San Francisco AI conference still ahead. Subscribe to keep those dates, and the Bay Area weeks, on your calendar.

author.name: Darren Su
author.bio: Co-founder of AGI Villa and MatchPoint; Head of City Ecosystem at Datawhale; n8n Ambassador.

bodyImages.alt: As of October 16, 2026: Reverie is still ahead in San Francisco, three builder conferences are still ahead in the Bay Area, and the Moscone and Fort Mason weeks have already been held

sections.heading: What I count as San Francisco
paragraphs: I put a row in the San Francisco table only when the organizer prints a date and a venue inside the city. Moscone, Fort Mason, Pier 48, and the Contemporary Jewish Museum count. The airport hotel in Burlingame, and the convention center in San Jose, go in the Bay Area section. I will not call Burlingame or San Jose a San Francisco trip because a homepage used that city name.

The program is AI-primary, or it is a major tech event whose official agenda is built around AI. I order each table by date. If the organizer site had no date when I read it on 2026-10-16, I left the event off. I am not filling a blank date.

sections.heading: What I would still book in the city
paragraphs: As of 2026-10-16, one AI conference is still ahead at a San Francisco venue. Reverie is a single day. LanceDB is the host, and the agenda is technical talks and breakouts for researchers and engineers. If you need a multi-day builder program that is still bookable, I would look outside the city, in the next section. I would not pretend Moscone still has an AI week left this year.

rows.bestFor: AI researchers, research engineers, and ML engineers
rows.aiFocus: Training data, world models, and multimodal systems
rows.costBand: $200 on the organizer page; a $125 tier ended Oct 9
rows.verdict: Go on November 5 if the work is training data, world models, or multimodal systems. The host is LanceDB, the room is the Contemporary Jewish Museum, and the agenda is technical talks and breakouts for researchers and engineers. Skip if you need a buyer hall or a Salesforce roadmap. Watch if the flight is tight. Selected stage talks are recorded afterward, and the breakouts are not. The organizer page lists $200. A $125 tier ended October 9.

sections.heading: Bay Area, still ahead
paragraphs: These three are still bookable as of 2026-10-16. None of them is in San Francisco. Open Source AI Week, October 16 to 25, is a Bay Area calendar of separately hosted events. The community site says it is not one conference, so I am not giving that week a Go or a Skip. The Linux Foundation names PyTorch Conference and AGNTCon + MCPCon as the flagship events of that week. Those two are rows. The week itself is not.

NVIDIA GTC is a San Jose event, and the 2026 edition has already run. The organizer page lists 2026 session replays and the next San Jose date as March 15 to 18, 2027. The GlobalTechEvents event guide records March 16 to 19, 2026 in San Jose. I left that week off both tables. If the product is the accelerator, open the NVIDIA GTC 2026 event guide in the list under What I would open next, then add the next cycle to your calendar.

table.caption: Still ahead in the Bay Area, outside San Francisco, as of 2026-10-16. Organizer dates only.

rows.city: San Jose Convention Center, 150 W San Carlos St
rows.aiFocus: Open-source deep learning, including PyTorch, vLLM, DeepSpeed, and Ray
rows.verdict: Go on October 20 to 21 if the work is PyTorch, or the open-source projects the Linux Foundation lists for this event: vLLM, DeepSpeed, and Ray, at the San Jose Convention Center. Skip the moment the trip has to be inside San Francisco. The FAQ says the conference is primarily in person, so I would not book it as a remote week.

rows.city: San Jose McEnery Convention Center, 150 W San Carlos St
rows.bestFor: Engineers building agents and MCP systems
rows.aiFocus: Open agentic AI and the Model Context Protocol
rows.verdict: Go on October 22 to 23, with the kickoff evening on October 21, if you ship agents or the Model Context Protocol. The Linux Foundation describes two days of keynotes, sessions, posters, and workshops at the San Jose McEnery Convention Center for builders, contributors, and enterprises in that ecosystem. Skip if you needed Moscone or a downtown San Francisco hotel. It uses the same San Jose convention center on the days after PyTorch Conference. I would not treat those two agendas as one trip.

rows.city: Hyatt Regency San Francisco Airport, 1333 Old Bayshore Hwy, Burlingame
rows.bestFor: Practitioners who want multi-day AI training
rows.aiFocus: Training tracks, an expo on Oct 27 to 28, and an AI X Leadership Summit on Oct 27 to 28
rows.verdict: Go on October 27 to 29 if you want those training days and can stay in Burlingame. The venue page address is the Hyatt Regency San Francisco Airport, 1333 Old Bayshore Hwy. Skip if you booked this as a Moscone week. The homepage also says San Francisco. I am using the venue address. Watch virtually only for the virtual sessions. The FAQ says in-person sessions are not livestreamed. The AI X Leadership Summit sits on October 27 to 28 inside this event, so a buyer who only wants that summit is a Watch.

sections.heading: Held in San Francisco
paragraphs: These 2026 editions used a San Francisco venue and have finished as of 2026-10-16. I would read a row only to decide whether the next edition earns a flight. Tech Week SF is not in the table. The organizer calls it a decentralized week of separately hosted events, and the FAQ dates are October 5 to 11, 2026. That week is over. I am not giving it a Go or a Skip.

table.caption: 2026 editions at a San Francisco venue that have already run, as of 2026-10-16. Organizer dates only.

rows.city: Moscone Center South, 747 Howard St, San Francisco
rows.bestFor: Executives and business leaders deciding how to use AI
rows.aiFocus: Enterprise AI adoption, policy, and operating practice
rows.verdict: Next cycle for a buyer who wants a leadership room on enterprise adoption, policy, and operating practice. The 2026 FAQ places April 6 to 9 at Moscone Center South, 747 Howard St. Skip if you needed engineering workshops on training systems. The same FAQ does not state a 2027 city, so I am not assuming another Moscone week.

rows.city: Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, and online
rows.verdict: Next cycle if you ship on Microsoft's agent and Azure stack. The Build live blog places June 2 to 3 in San Francisco and online, and names Fort Mason for the in-person event. Skip if you came for GPUs or a startup expo. If the keynotes were the point, I would watch the session catalog on the Build site. Fort Mason also hosted OpenAI DevDay in September, and that does not make this the OpenAI week.

rows.city: Moscone Center, San Francisco, plus a virtual track
rows.bestFor: Data engineers, scientists, and teams on Databricks
rows.verdict: Next cycle if the job is the Databricks platform: lakehouse, governance, analytics, and agents. The June 2, 2026 press release says June 15 to 18 at Moscone, in person and virtual. Skip if that platform is not yours. I would not send a model-lab team here and call it close enough. The current summit site lists the next edition as June 21 to 24, 2027 at Moscone North, West, and South.

rows.city: Moscone West, 747 Howard Street, San Francisco
rows.aiFocus: Applied AI workshops and technical tracks
rows.verdict: Next cycle for engineers who want applied AI workshops and technical tracks. The organizer FAQ says June 29 through July 2 at Moscone West, 747 Howard Street, and says talks are being released on its YouTube channel. Watch the recordings if you cannot fly. Moscone's own listing prints June 30 to July 2. I am using the organizer span. A leadership ticket existed, so a buyer is a Watch, until you read that agenda. I would not treat this as the paper week.

rows.city: Moscone Center, San Francisco, and Salesforce+
rows.aiFocus: Agentforce, CRM, and enterprise AI on that platform
rows.verdict: Next cycle only when the purchase is Salesforce: Agentforce, CRM, and enterprise AI on that platform. The registration page says September 15 to 17, 2026 at Moscone, with a Salesforce+ broadcast. Skip for GPU teams and for API teams outside that estate. The organizer says sessions are on demand on Salesforce+. The same site lists September 21 to 23, 2027 in San Francisco. I would not book it because it is the famous Moscone week.

Next cycle only if you ship on OpenAI: models, APIs, Codex, and agents. The DevDay FAQ says September 29, 2026 at Fort Mason. Skip if your platform is a different API. Microsoft Build used the same building in June, and I would not treat the two as one stack. Watch the recap. The keynote was livestreamed, and OpenAI said other sessions would be posted on openai.com.

rows.bestFor: Builders, researchers, and startup teams who can attend in person
rows.aiFocus: Applied AI, agents, infrastructure, and an on-site startup program
rows.verdict: Next cycle if you wanted that in-person mix of builders, researchers, and startup teams: applied AI, agents, infrastructure, and an on-site startup program. The organizer FAQ says September 29 through October 1 at Pier 48, Mission Rock, in person only. Skip if you needed a livestream. It shares September 29 with DevDay at Fort Mason. One is an OpenAI API day. This one is in person only at Pier 48. I would not book them as one trip. The homepage lists a save-the-date of October 12 to 14, 2027 in San Francisco, without a street address on that line. I am not claiming a 2026 recording.

rows.city: Moscone West, 800 Howard St, San Francisco
rows.aiFocus: Startup conference with AI sessions, not an AI-only program
rows.verdict: Already over. The attendee portal says October 13 to 15 at Moscone West, 800 Howard St. Next cycle for founder and investor density. Skip if you needed a research venue or a training workshop. The official frame is a startup conference with AI sessions. I would not send a PyTorch engineer here and call the badge close enough.

sections.heading: Who I would send
paragraphs: I pick from the role that matches the trip. I fill a cell only when the organizer site states the audience or the format. A thin agenda stays at Watch.

subsections.heading: AI and platform engineers
paragraphs: Still ahead, I would book Reverie on November 5 if the work is training data or multimodal models, and that is the only day I would still book inside the city. I would book PyTorch Conference on October 20 to 21 if the work is that open-source stack, and AGNTCon + MCPCon on October 22 to 23 if the work is agents or MCP. Both of those are in San Jose. I would book ODSC AI West on October 27 to 29 only if Burlingame is an acceptable venue for training days. Already held, and worth a next-cycle look only on a matching stack: AI Engineer World's Fair for applied engineering workshops, Microsoft Build for the Microsoft agent and Azure stack, OpenAI DevDay for the OpenAI API, Databricks if the platform is Databricks. Build and DevDay both used Fort Mason. I would not stack them. They are different APIs.

subsections.heading: Founders and go-to-market
paragraphs: Reverie is a skip when the goal is buyer density. LanceDB is hosting a technical day for researchers and engineers, not a fundraising floor. TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13 to 15 at Moscone West, was the startup and investor week, and it has ended. Dreamforce was the Salesforce buyer week, and it has ended. I would not use one as a substitute for the other. Tech Week SF, October 5 to 11, was a week of separately hosted events, and it has ended. I am not scoring that week.

subsections.heading: Enterprise buyers
paragraphs: Dreamforce is the Salesforce week. Sessions from the 2026 edition are on Salesforce+, and the organizer lists September 21 to 23, 2027 in San Francisco. HumanX, April 6 to 9 at Moscone South, is the leadership week that has already run. I would not send a Databricks team there for lakehouse training. Databricks is the lakehouse week. ODSC lists an AI X Leadership Summit on October 27 to 28 inside the Burlingame event. That is the buyer slice still ahead, and it is not a Moscone buyer hall. I would book the estate you are actually buying.

subsections.heading: Researchers
paragraphs: Reverie is the technical day still ahead in the city. It is a LanceDB summit on training data, world models, and multimodal systems. NeurIPS, ICML, and CVPR are the paper venues. I am not assigning them a 2026 city here, and I am not ranking them against Reverie. AI Engineer World's Fair and The AI Conference were in-person San Francisco programs with research-adjacent talks, and both have ended. The AI Conference FAQ says that event is in person only. A paper venue is a different job, and I am not using this page to pick one.

sections.heading: What I would open next
paragraphs: Open the San Francisco city page when you want every tech event this calendar lists in the city. Open an event guide when you want dates for one conference. Subscribe to the ICS feed, or join WhatsApp, when you want those dates on a calendar without waiting for me to revise this article. The list under this section is the city page, the AI hubs, and the event guides that already exist. The links after the FAQ also include the organizer sites I used for the dates above. Confirm the organizer page before you book a flight.

faq.question: Which San Francisco AI conferences are still upcoming in 2026?
faq.answer: As of 2026-10-16, I would still book Reverie on November 5 at the Contemporary Jewish Museum, and that is the only AI conference still ahead inside San Francisco. PyTorch Conference on October 20 to 21 and AGNTCon + MCPCon on October 22 to 23 are still ahead in San Jose. ODSC AI West on October 27 to 29 is still ahead in Burlingame. The Moscone and Fort Mason editions on this page have already run.

faq.question: Is San Jose or the SFO airport hotel the same as San Francisco for this guide?
faq.answer: No. When I say San Francisco I mean a venue in the city, such as Moscone, Fort Mason, Pier 48, or the Contemporary Jewish Museum. ODSC AI West is at the Hyatt Regency San Francisco Airport, 1333 Old Bayshore Hwy, Burlingame. PyTorch Conference and AGNTCon + MCPCon are at the San Jose Convention Center. NVIDIA lists the next GTC in San Jose. I would book those as Bay Area trips.

faq.question: How do I pick one San Francisco AI trip this quarter?
faq.answer: The conference I would still book inside the city is Reverie, one day on November 5, and only for researchers and engineers working on training data. A multi-day builder program that is still bookable is in San Jose or Burlingame. Dreamforce, DevDay, Build, the Data + AI Summit, HumanX, AI Engineer World's Fair, The AI Conference, and Disrupt have already run in 2026. I would use the held table when you are planning the next cycle of one of those.

faq.question: Where do I get the dates on a calendar?
faq.answer: Subscribe to the GlobalTechEvents ICS feed at /api/calendar, or join the WhatsApp group linked on this page. I dated this article 2026-10-16. Check the organizer site before you book, because a homepage can move on to next year's dates while this table still describes 2026.
